subject: FinHealth — Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finhealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@finhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: FinHealth — Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps

Hi Tom / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Great conversation — below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please correct me where I missed anything.

Key pain points / drivers
- Regulated PHI/PII workloads: cannot send inference traffic to a public shared control plane; need data residency in US-only.
- Strong requirement for customer-managed key material (KMS/HSM) and key rotation policies.
- Network constraints: egress restrictions, strict firewall rules, and desire for either VPC peering/PrivateLink or air-gapped on-prem option for production.
- Auditability: SOC2 evidence, detailed audit logs for every inference request, and Splunk integration for SIEM.
- Procurement: legal needs SOC2 artifacts and a short statement on data handling before signing.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Models / serving: in-house model endpoints on AWS EKS today (GPU-backed nodes).
- Identity / KMS: AWS KMS-managed keys for data-at-rest; company policy requires HSM-backed keys and 90-day rotation for production keys.
- Network: Transit Gateway in us-east-1, strict outbound egress via proxy, IDS/IPS managed by MSSP.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
- No customer data leaves FinHealth-managed VPCs (control plane either deployed to their VPC or private connectivity with zero public egress).
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM integration with enforced rotation.
- P95 inference latency <= 250ms for our expected burst profile (baseline: 150–200 rps sustained, 800 rps burst).
- SOC2 artifacts and proof of logging/audit before procurement sign-off.

Proposed technical approach (options we discussed)
1) Redwood Private (VPC-hosted) — private control plane deployed into FinHealth VPC; uses AWS PrivateLink / VPC peering for control plane -> worker communication; customer supplies KMS keys (alias) and we integrate using role-based access with no key export.
2) Dedicated Private with HSM — similar to (1) but keys stored in customer HSM; we operate under a customer-managed IAM role for signing/calls.
3) Air-gapped on-prem appliance (proof-of-concept) — full offline install with limited telemetry; recommended for highest compliance environments.

Attachments I shared
- FinHealth_network_requirements.xlsx (network ports, CIDRs, firewall rules)
- SOC2-summary.pdf (high level compliance artifacts)
- redwood-private-arch.png (proposed connectivity diagram)

Next steps
- Tom/Priya: confirm network diagram and add any missing CIDRs or proxy requirements (deadline: 2026-07-05).
- FinHealth: confirm KMS/HSM vendor and rotation policy details (90-day rotation requirement noted).
- Schedule technical deep-dive with our solutions engineering (Aditya) and DevOps (Dev). We proposed Thu 2026-07-08 10:00am PT or Fri 2026-07-09 9:00am PT — please confirm.
- I'll circulate a short checklist for procurement/legal listing the SOC2 artifacts we can provide and the timeline.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through the diagram.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — really appreciate the clear summary. Quick clarifications / items to add: 

- Procurement timeline: aiming to finalize vendor selection by end of July; procurement/legal will need SOC2 Type II reports and a short data-handling statement before they can move forward.
- Security: we use Splunk for SIEM and will need an integration plan for audit logs. MSSP requires a signed runbook for incident response.
- KMS/HSM: we currently use AWS CloudHSM for certain keys; any solution must support HSM-backed keys and automated rotation (rotation cadence: 90 days).
- Network: we can't accept any public IP egress from production; PrivateLink or TGW peering preferred. Also our proxy terminates TLS for outbound; any inbound connections from Redwood must be explicitly listed in the firewall spreadsheet.

Can you also call out whether Redwood's private control plane requires outbound connections to external telemetry endpoints? We need that explicitly described for our security team.

I'll review the attached network workbook and send a completed version by Friday.

-Tom

Subject: Re: FinHealth — Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps

Tom — thanks, noted and totally understood. Looping in Aditya (solutions engineering) and Dev (platform) to run the technical deep dive and answer the detailed security questions.

To answer your telemetry question up-front: in our standard Private offering we can operate with zero egress to public telemetry endpoints. There are three modes to be explicit: 
- Fully private (recommended): control plane deployed in your VPC, no public egress; logs and metrics are exported to your Splunk/CloudWatch via customer-managed collectors.
- Private with opt-in telemetry: minimal encrypted heartbeat to Redwood for health/alerting; can be disabled for compliance.
- Air-gapped on-prem: no external connectivity; we deliver a signed installer and limited offline telemetry (customer pulls logs for Redwood support).

Key technical notes:
- KMS/HSM: we support AWS KMS + CloudHSM for key storage and can integrate with customer HSMs where the customer retains key ownership (we never export the private key). Rotation can be automated via your existing KMS rotation policies.
- Connectivity options: VPC peering / Transit Gateway (recommended for low-latency) or AWS PrivateLink (when you want endpoint-level control). We'll document required ports in the workbook.
- Logging: full request/response audit logs can be forwarded to your Splunk instance; PII redaction policies can be applied at ingestion.
- SLA / perf: our initial sizing suggests we can meet the P95 <= 250ms target for the stated workload with a Dedicated pool; we'll confirm after the deep-dive and a short load-profile test.

Aditya / Dev: suggested agenda for the deep dive (30–45m):
1) Walk through updated network workbook (CIDRs, proxy, NAT, egress rules).
2) KMS/HSM integration details and key rotation flow.
3) Logging/Splunk ingestion and runbook for incident response.
4) Deployment model options (Private vs air-gapped) and offline support requirements.
5) Next steps: timeline for POC and procurement artifacts.

Proposed meeting times (PT): Thu 2026-07-08 10:00 or Fri 2026-07-09 09:00. If neither works, suggest a couple of alternatives and we'll coordinate. I've also attached a short checklist for procurement that lists the SOC2 artifacts we can provide.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
